html:
The Inga are an Indigenous people of southwest Colombia, in the Sibundoy valley of Putumayo and nearby Nariño and Cauca. Unusually for Colombia, they speak a form of Quechua, the language of the Inca Empire.

How they came to speak it is debated. One view is that they descend from settlers or traders moved north under Inca rule; another is that Quechua spread as a trade language. They share the Sibundoy valley with the Kamëntsá, who speak an unrelated language. Inga healers are widely known for their knowledge of medicinal plants, including yagé (ayahuasca), and travelled far as herbalists. Their neighbours to the south include the Siona and the Pasto.
